title: Sample Five
description: Five small surprises, from ocean hearts to the internet’s first hello. A reusable sample round for testing Today’s Five.

cards.hook: Eight arms. An even stranger heartbeat.
cards.question: An octopus has eight arms. How many hearts keep them going?
cards.revealHeadline: Three hearts. One very busy octopus.
cards.explanation: Two hearts move blood through the gills to pick up oxygen. The third sends that oxygen-rich blood around the body. Its copper-based oxygen carrier, hemocyanin, also gives the blood a blue color.

cards.hook: Woody and Buzz helped change how movies are made.
cards.question: What made Toy Story a first when it reached cinemas in 1995?
choices: The first feature with stop-motion puppets
The first animated feature with recorded dialogue
The first animated feature shown in color
cards.revealHeadline: A whole feature, built with computer animation.
cards.explanation: Toy Story was the first feature-length movie made entirely with computer animation. Pixar brought Woody, Buzz, and their world to the screen with digitally rendered images.

sources.publisher: Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences
sources.title: Toy Story

cards.hook: The Red Planet has a surprise at sundown.
cards.question: You are watching sunset on Mars. What color glow can appear around the Sun?
cards.revealHeadline: The Red Planet gets a blue sunset glow.
cards.explanation: Fine dust in the Martian atmosphere scatters light differently from the air on Earth. Near sunset, blue light stays concentrated toward the Sun while much of the surrounding sky looks yellow, orange, or reddish.

sources.title: NASA’s Curiosity Rover Views Serene Sundown on Mars

cards.hook: A snack with a tiny pressure-cooker secret.
cards.question: What makes a popcorn kernel pop when you heat it?
choices: Oil boils inside a thin skin
Trapped air makes the shell melt
Water becomes vapor inside a tough hull
cards.canonicalAnswer: Water becomes vapor inside a tough hull
cards.revealHeadline: Every kernel is a tiny pressure cooker.
cards.explanation: A popcorn kernel holds moisture inside a strong outer hull. As the water heats and vaporizes, pressure builds until the hull bursts. The softened starch expands outward into the fluffy snack.

sources.title: What’s under the shell of this popular snack?

cards.hook: Even the internet’s first conversation hit a snag.
cards.question: In 1969, UCLA tried to send LOGIN over ARPANET. Which letters arrived before the system crashed?
cards.explanation: The L and O reached the computer at Stanford Research Institute before the system crashed. The team restored the connection and successfully sent the full command later that evening.

sources.title: Pioneers and Visionaries to Celebrate Internet's 50th Anniversary at UCLA
